<h1 class="h1">Operating Systems</h1>
<p class="role">CS 301 · IIT Gandhinagar · Semester I, 2018–19</p>
<p class="lede" style="margin-top:18px">CS 301 is an introduction to operating systems, organised around the three parts of the textbook: virtualisation of the CPU and memory, concurrency, and persistence. Every lecture links its slides and, for most lectures, the class recording. Labs and homework are hands-on work in C and Python on Linux.</p>
<dl class="facts">
  <dt>Instructor</dt><dd><a href="https://nipunbatra.github.io">Prof. Nipun Batra</a></dd>

  <dt>Labs</dt><dd>Wednesday</dd>

</dl>

<div class="two rule-top">
<section id="faq"><h2>Questions</h2>
<details class="q" id="textbook"><summary>Which textbook does the course follow?</summary><p><a href="http://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~remzi/OSTEP/">Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces</a> by Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau and Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau, which is free online. The course follows its three parts, and many lab and homework questions come from its chapters.</p></details>
<details class="q" id="setup"><summary>What software do I need?</summary><p>Linux, either native or in a virtual machine, with GCC, GDB and htop, and Python 3 from Anaconda. The course provides an <a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jZVQRuomuYsuK5dkTyuVMxV4oNLFX8Hs/view">Ubuntu VirtualBox image</a>.</p></details>
<details class="q" id="homework"><summary>How is homework submitted?</summary><p>As a typed PDF uploaded on the form, named <code>{branch}_{roll_number}_{name}.pdf</code>, with all code linked as secret GitHub gists. Deadlines are at noon and are hard: the form closes and there are no extensions. See <a href="assignments.html">Homework</a>.</p></details>
<details class="q" id="project"><summary>Is there a project?</summary><p>Yes. Project ideas are collected in a <a href="https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1eVVmBrCTXHa6XhfewG2S9_if11Ija0s_cNMBp5NMbww/edit?usp=sharing">shared spreadsheet</a>, a demo or a video has to be shown in class, and projects were graded in rounds. See <a href="assessment.html#project">Project</a>.</p></details>
<details class="q" id="code"><summary>Where is the code shown in class?</summary><p>In the <a href="code/index.html">code folder</a>: process API examples, scheduling and memory simulators, and thread examples, many of them from the textbook's own code.</p></details>
</section>
